Purpose: Analysis of James Woodworth Prairie 2022-2023 flux data. Led by Junior Francois with supervision of Gavin McNicol at the University of Illinois Chicago. Below, N2O fluxes are removed from the analysis due to unusually poor precision on the McNicol Lab gas chromatograph. CO2 and CH4 fluxes are retained after QAQC screening.

# Initial Slope-Flux QAQC and Calculation

**Logic table:**

Situation,                                  CO2,  CH4,  N2O
CO2 flag == "bad" OR if slope is negative   NA,   NA,   NA
CO2 flag == "ok", but CH4/N2O flag == "bad" keep, 0,    0
CO2 flag == "ok", and CH4/N2O flag == "ok"  keep, keep, keep

*Set very high woodland CO2 emissions (> 9) related to ant burrow to `NA`

```{r flux-qc}
data <- data %>%
  group_by(date, site, zone, chamber_no) %>%
  mutate(
    # Extract the CO2 values for this chamber measurement
    co2_flag   = flag[gas == "co2"][1],
    co2_slope_ppm_min  = slope_ppm_min[gas == "co2"][1],
    
    # Flag bad analytical process / injection based on CO2
    bad_injection = (is.na(co2_flag) | co2_flag == "bad") |
                    co2_slope_ppm_min < 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    slope_ppm_min = case_when(
      # Everything from a bad injection becomes NA
      bad_injection ~ NA_real_,
      
      # CO2 that passed the checks keeps its value
      gas == "co2" ~ slope_ppm_min,
      
      # CH4 / N2O with non-significant slope → 0 (only if injection was good)
      gas %in% c("ch4", "n2o") & flag == "bad" ~ 0,
      
      # Otherwise keep the calculated flux
      TRUE ~ slope_ppm_min
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-co2_flag, -co2_slope_ppm_min, -bad_injection, -r2, -y_intercept, -flag, -Comment) %>%
  ungroup()
```

get chamber vols and temps

```{r}
vols <- read_csv("data/chamber_vols.csv") %>% select(site, zone = ecosystem, chamber_no, vol_m3 = total_vol_m3)
temps <- read_csv("data/chamber_temps.csv") %>% select(date, site, zone = ecosystem_name, chamber_no, chamber_temp = average_temp_kelvin) %>% mutate(date = ymd(date))
```
join to data
fill NA temps with mean temp
fill NA vols with mean vol

```{r}
data <- data %>% 
  left_join(vols) %>% left_join(temps)

mean(data$vol_m3, na.rm = T)
mean(data$chamber_temp, na.rm = T)

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(vol_m3 = case_when(
    is.na(vol_m3) ~ 0.0133,
    TRUE ~ vol_m3
  )) %>% 
  mutate(chamber_temp = case_when(
    is.na(chamber_temp) ~ 299.09,
    TRUE ~ chamber_temp
  ))
```

calculate fluxes

```{r fluxes-ideal-gas}
# Constants
P_atm <- 1                      # assume 1 atm unless you have barometric data
R     <- 8.205736e-5            # m3 atm mol-1 K-1
diam_cm <- 25.4                 # chamber diameter
area_m2 <- pi * (diam_cm / 100 / 2)^2   # 0.05067075 m2

# flux_df should already have:
# date, site, zone, chamber_no, gas, slope_ppm_min, vol_m3, chamber_temp (K)

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    gas = str_to_lower(gas),
    area_m2 = area_m2,
    # mol gas in chamber per ppm
    mol_per_ppm = (P_atm * vol_m3) / (R * chamber_temp) * 1e-6,
    # mol m-2 s-1
    flux_mol_m2_s = mol_per_ppm * (slope_ppm_min / 60) / area_m2,
    flux = case_when(
      gas == "co2" ~ flux_mol_m2_s * 1e6,   # umol m-2 s-1
      gas %in% c("ch4", "n2o") ~ flux_mol_m2_s * 1e9,  # nmol m-2 s-1
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    flux_units = case_when(
      gas == "co2" ~ "umol m-2 s-1",
      gas %in% c("ch4", "n2o") ~ "nmol m-2 s-1",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(date, site, zone, chamber_no, gas,
         slope_ppm_min, vol_m3, chamber_temp, area_m2,
         flux, flux_units)
```


```{r detection-limit}
# ============================================================
# Lowest Detectable Flux for CH4 and N2O
# ============================================================

# ---- Instrument precision ----
ch4_std_ppm    <- 10.1      # ppm
n2o_std_ppm    <- 1.0       # ppm
rel_precision  <- 0.02      # 2%

ch4_precision_ppm <- ch4_std_ppm * rel_precision   # 0.303 ppm
n2o_precision_ppm <- n2o_std_ppm * rel_precision   # 0.030 ppm

# ---- Chamber parameters ----
area_m2   <- 0.05          # m²
height_m  <- 0.12          # m
time_min  <- 30            # minutes
time_s    <- time_min * 60

# ---- Ideal gas conversion (ppm → nmol m⁻³) ----
# At 1 atm and 25 °C:
# 1 ppm = 40.87 µmol m⁻³ = 40870 nmol m⁻³
R <- 0.082057              # L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹
T <- 298.15                # K
P <- 1                     # atm

moles_per_m3     <- (P / (R * T)) * 1000          # mol m⁻³
ppm_to_nmol_m3   <- moles_per_m3 * 1000           # nmol m⁻³ per ppm
# ≈ 40870

# ---- Minimum detectable flux ----
# F (nmol m⁻² s⁻¹) = (ΔC_nmol_m3 / Δt_s) * height_m

ch4_min_flux <- (ch4_precision_ppm * ppm_to_nmol_m3 / time_s) * height_m
n2o_min_flux <- (n2o_precision_ppm * ppm_to_nmol_m3 / time_s) * height_m

# ---- Results ----
cat("=== Lowest Detectable Flux ===\n")
cat(sprintf("CH4 precision          : %.3f ppm\n", ch4_precision_ppm))
cat(sprintf("CH4 lowest detectable flux : %.3f nmol m⁻² s⁻¹\n\n", ch4_min_flux))

cat(sprintf("N2O precision          : %.3f ppm\n", n2o_precision_ppm))
cat(sprintf("N2O lowest detectable flux : %.3f nmol m⁻² s⁻¹\n", n2o_min_flux))

cat("\nAssumptions used:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Chamber area     = %.3f m²\n", area_m2))
cat(sprintf("  Chamber height   = %.2f m\n", height_m))
cat(sprintf("  Deployment time  = %.0f min\n", time_min))
cat("  Temperature/pressure ≈ 25 °C, 1 atm\n")
```

# Microtopographic zone effects

Q: is there a significant zone effect?

Problem with linear models: outliers may distort model behavior for CH4

Check the effects with influence eval on full model with all data

Flag outlier first
```{r}
ch4 <- data %>% filter(gas == "ch4", !is.na(flux))

# A) global fence (what you used)
q <- quantile(ch4$flux, c(0.25, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE)
iqr <- diff(q)
ch4_lower <- q[1] - 1.5 * iqr
ch4_upper <- q[2] + 1.5 * iqr

# B) zone-wise fence (matches left-column boxplots)
ch4_flagged <- ch4 %>%
  group_by(zone) %>%
  mutate(
    q1 = quantile(flux, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q3 = quantile(flux, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_z = q3 - q1,
    outlier_zone = flux < q1 - 1.5 * iqr_z | flux > q3 + 1.5 * iqr_z,
    outlier_global = flux < ch4_lower | flux > ch4_upper,
    direction = case_when(
      flux > 0 ~ "emission",
      flux < 0 ~ "uptake",
      TRUE ~ "zero"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

ch4_flagged %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_zone = sum(outlier_zone),
    n_global = sum(outlier_global),
    pct_zone = 100 * n_zone / n,
    pct_global = 100 * n_global / n
  )
```

OK, more within-zone outliers than global, so within-zone is better flagger

```{r}
outliers <- ch4_flagged %>% filter(outlier_zone)

# counts by zone and sign
outliers %>%
  count(zone, direction, name = "n") %>%
  group_by(zone) %>%
  mutate(pct_of_zone_outliers = 100 * n / sum(n))

# are they clustered in time?
outliers %>%
  mutate(year = year(date),
         month = month(date)) %>% 
  count(zone, year, month, direction) %>%
  arrange(year, month, zone)

# magnitude
outliers %>%
  group_by(zone, direction) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    min = min(flux),
    median = median(flux),
    max = max(flux),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}

```


Mostly emission outliers, and mostly in SW-1

```{r}
fit_all <- lm(flux ~ zone + factor(year) + factor(month),
              data = filter(data, gas == "ch4") %>% 
                mutate(year  = year(date),
                       month = month(date)))

fit_no  <- lm(flux ~ zone + factor(year) + factor(month),
              data = ch4_flagged %>% 
                mutate(year  = year(date),
                       month = month(date)) %>% 
                filter(!outlier_zone))
              
pairs(emmeans(fit_all, ~ zone), adjust = "tukey")
pairs(emmeans(fit_no,  ~ zone), adjust = "tukey")
```

check influence of outliers

```{r}
diag <- broom::augment(fit_all) %>%
  mutate(
    cook_cut = 4 / n(),
    student_cut = 3,
    influential = .cooksd > cook_cut | abs(.std.resid) > student_cut
  )

diag %>%
  filter(influential) %>%
  count(zone)

# compare
lm(flux ~ zone + `factor(year)` + `factor(month)`,
   data = diag %>% filter(!influential))
```


## Interpretation of outlier analysis

Of 212 CH₄ fluxes, 29 (14%) fell outside a zone-wise 1.5×IQR fence. These were not clustered on a single date: 19 were in SW-1 (11 emission, 8 uptake), 5 were strong 2022 uptake in UP-1, and 5 were in SW-2 or UP-2. A global 1.5×IQR fence flagged 20 points (9%). SW-1’s high outlier count reflects a near-zero IQR at or below the CH₄ detection limit (0.55 nmol m⁻² s⁻¹), not erroneous chambers. These IQR flags were used only to describe the tails and to examine how they inflate residual variance in the linear model (Table Sx). They were not used as an exclusion rule. Influence diagnostics identified three points (two SW-1, one SW-2) with Cook’s D > 4/n or |studentized residual| > 3. Only those three observations were removed before fitting the CH₄ model and Tukey HSD tests.

### influential points

```{r}
outliers %>%
  group_by(zone, direction) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    min = min(flux), median = median(flux), max = max(flux),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# the only points that matter for the lm
diag %>%
  filter(influential) %>%
  select(zone, year = `factor(year)`, month = `factor(month)`, flux, .std.resid, .cooksd)
```

## Tukey's HSD for main figure

make temp data with factors

```{r}
tukey_dat <- lm_data %>% 
  mutate(year = year(date),
   month = month(date)) %>% 
  mutate(flux = case_when(
    year == 2023 & month == 3 ~ NA,
    TRUE ~ flux
  )) %>% 
  mutate(year  = factor(year),
    month = factor(month))

tukey_dat_co2 <- tukey_dat %>% 
  filter(gas == "co2")

tukey_dat_ch4 <- tukey_dat %>% 
  filter(gas == "ch4")

fit_co2 <- lm(flux ~ zone + year + month, data = tukey_dat_co2)
fit_ch4 <- lm(flux ~ zone + year + month, data = tukey_dat_ch4)
```

# soil moisture and temperature QCQA

```{r}
            moist_lower = mean(soil_moist) - 3 * sd(soil_moist)/sqrt(4),
            temp_upper = mean(soil_temp) + 3 * sd(soil_temp)/sqrt(4),
            temp_lower = mean(soil_temp) - 3 * sd(soil_temp)/sqrt(4)
            )
```

# PARIO Filtering bad rows, replace with adjacent layer means

```{r replace-bad-texture}
# Failed / suspect layers from the PARIO QC
# SW-1 80, SW-2 50, UP-1 0, UP-1 40, UP-2 0 (suspect), UP-2 20
bad <- tibble(
  zone  = c("SW-1", "SW-2", "UP-1", "UP-1", "UP-2", "UP-2"),
  depth = c(80,     50,     0,      40,     0,      20)
)

neighbor_mean <- function(dat, z, d) {
  nbr <- dat |>
    filter(zone == z, depth %in% c(d - 10, d + 10))
  if (nrow(nbr) == 0) {
    stop("No adjoining layers for ", z, " depth ", d)
  }
  nbr |>
    summarise(
      sand = mean(sand),
      silt = mean(silt),
      clay = mean(clay)
    )
}

fixed <- c_stocks
for (i in seq_len(nrow(bad))) {
  z <- bad$zone[i]
  d <- bad$depth[i]
  repl <- neighbor_mean(c_stocks, z, d)   # means from the original (unedited) table
  fixed <- fixed |>
    mutate(
      sand = ifelse(zone == z & depth == d, repl$sand, sand),
      silt = ifelse(zone == z & depth == d, repl$silt, silt),
      clay = ifelse(zone == z & depth == d, repl$clay, clay)
    )
}

# sanity check: only those 6 rows should change, and only texture
compare <- c_stocks |>
  inner_join(fixed, by = c("zone", "depth"), suffix = c("_old", "_new")) |>
  filter(sand_old != sand_new | silt_old != silt_new | clay_old != clay_new) |>
  select(zone, depth, starts_with("sand"), starts_with("silt"), starts_with("clay"))

compare

# write if you want a new file
write_csv(fixed, "tidy-data/soc-stocks-texture-filled.csv")
```

# bulk density estimation method

```{r}
set.seed (12567)

library(randomForestSRC)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(grid)
library(gridExtra)
library(clhs)
library(caret)
library(terra)

########## Import the package dataset to build PTF
load("env-data/soil/Geo_Peds06132016.Rda")

#Subset pedons for depth less than 200 cm
Peds_200 <- subset(Geo_Peds, Geo_Peds$depth <= 200)

# Extract BD model variables
fm = bd ~ soc + ph_h2o + sand + clay + depth + structsize + structtype + surf_geology + province + hzn_desg

## Missing values distribution:
sel <- (Peds_200[,all.vars(fm)])
summary(sel)

# Extract complete cases for comparison
sel.complete <- complete.cases(sel)
summary(sel.complete)

## 41,878 complete (or 20%)
Peds_complete <- sel[sel.complete,]

# Create latin hypercube sample with 50% of complete data (50% selected for speed)
cs <- clhs(Peds_complete, size  = nrow(Peds_complete)/2, progress = FALSE, simple = FALSE)

# Create calibration dataframe of latin hypercube samples
calib_data <- cs$sampled_data
rfsrc_BD <- rfsrc(fm, data=calib_data, ntree=150)
```

```{r}
texture_summary <- fixed %>%
```

```{r co2-decision-tree}
d <- data_soil %>%
  filter(gas == "co2") %>%
  mutate(
    zone = factor(zone)
  ) %>%
  select(flux, soil_temp, soil_moist, sand, silt, clay, carbon, nitrogen, zone) %>%
  na.omit()

tree_mod <- rpart(
  flux ~ soil_temp + soil_moist + sand + silt + clay + carbon + nitrogen + zone,
  data = d,
  method = "anova",
  control = rpart.control(
    cp = 0.03,
    minsplit = 10,
    minbucket = 5
  )
)

 summary(tree_mod)
```

```{r co2-tree-eval}
# get best error
best_cp <- tree_mod$cptable[
  which.min(tree_mod$cptable[, "xerror"]),
  "CP"
]

best_cp

# prune tree
tree_pruned <- prune(tree_mod, cp = best_cp)

rpart.plot(tree_pruned)

printcp(tree_pruned)

# Training R²
pred <- predict(tree_pruned)
R2_train <- cor(d$flux, pred)^2

# Cross-validated R²
R2_cv <- 1 - min(tree_pruned$cptable[, "xerror"])

R2_train; R2_cv

tree_pruned$variable.importance/517.99614
```

nsplits = 6
CO2 CV R2 = 1-0.5202714 = 0.48
Rel. Err. = 0.33

# more within node stats (change tree by creating/re-creating `tree_pruned`)

```{r}
node_stats <- tree_pruned$frame %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("node") %>%
  filter(var == "<leaf>") %>%          # keep only terminal nodes
  mutate(
    n          = n,
    mean       = yval,                 # predicted value (node mean)
    sse        = dev,                  # sum of squared errors
    variance   = dev / n,              # population variance
    sd         = sqrt(dev / n),        # within-node standard deviation
    se         = sd / sqrt(n)          # standard error of the mean
  ) %>%
  select(node, n, mean, sd, se)

print(node_stats)
```
